The example plot. After the NDA you receive the full list of plots, each with its own sheet and simulation of the figures. The figures vary with each plot's specifics; everything is transparent before any decision.

Why
  • Value uplift: we invest to take the plot to ready-to-build (masterplan, PUZ, permits, access, utilities) and capture the uplift
  • Leverage: we lock the plot with a 10% deposit, refundable and secured, and capture the upside on 100% of the land value at the end
  • Know-how: we have the strategic architect and the full picture: the PUG, the infrastructure, the related developments and the development criteria in the area; the PUZ is built around them
  • The buyer gets something clear: what they can build, how much and when they can start
  • De-risking: we sell the SPV before the balance of the price is due; we take the upside without the development risk, and development stays on the table as an option
  • Several monetisation routes: we can also be the buyers for development; the others under monetisation
How
  • One dedicated SPV: Tunari Land Invest 1 S.R.L.
  • 10% deposit: refundable on demand and secured by mortgage
  • Risk: 5% maximum of the land value, the operating budget
  • Investors provide the capital: the deposit + the budget of 5% maximum
  • RBI Land delivers at a fixed price and earns only after investors have recovered all their capital
Investors' capital comes back first.
The gain is split 70 / 30.

The area: we come before, not after

context

The plot sits between the airport, the A0 ring motorway and DJ200B, on the corridor where public investment north of Bucharest is concentrating. The development pole is moving from Otopeni towards A0: from here you reach the ring and, through it, the whole of Bucharest. The option is taken now, at farmland prices, not after the works are finished.

Zone A · highest interest: between DJ200B, the express road and A0; the 6 ha example plot is here
Zone B · Dimieni, along the express road, between the airport and A0
Zone C · below the airport, between the express road, DJ200B and DN1

The airport expands towards Tunari

  • Terminal 2: design contract signed on 30 June 2026 with the consortium led by Leviatan Design (18.4 M €); 30 million passengers a year, 176,000 sqm; design 2 years, construction 3.5 years
  • Runway 1: ≈ 106 M €, being awarded
  • Investment announced at Otopeni up to 2030: ≈ 1.8 billion € (CNAB)
  • Airport logistics, hotels, parking, retailers and a retail gallery as anchor: the buyers for the plots we lock

Roads, from three directions

  • CNAIR: the A0 – Terminal 2 express road, 2.55 km plus 7.5 km of ramps, ≈ 80 M €, budget approved, 15 bids under evaluation; 30 months from signing (6 design + 24 build); A0 to the airport in 2 minutes. When the road is done, the first step of land value next to it is collected
  • Ilfov County: DJ200B widened to 3 lanes and the DJ100 junction reorganised, funding approved
  • Tunari town hall: local streets (Rândunicii, Zborului, Air City), modernisation under way
  • Later: the new terminal's rail link, provided for in the project

Demand and prices

  • Amber Forest (Alesonor): ≈ 200 M € invested, second phase under construction; land bought at around 10 €/sqm, plots selling today at ≈ 300 €/sqm. Along 23 August boulevard in Otopeni, both sides, the same story
  • City Nord: 13 projects, 8 completed and 5 under way, plus 4 plots on 11 ha in PUZ; Nusco Homes, in the same area: land bought at ≈ 40 €/sqm four years ago, selling today at ≈ 180 €/sqm; the community exists, the demand for plots comes from there
  • Comparable land, without a PUZ, is listed today in the area at 55–70 €/sqm; west of DJ200B, 90–220 €/sqm. We buy at 20 and sell at 40: plots not yet validated, ahead of the road. The financial projection is explained plot by plot, in each plot's file
  • We do not promise that whole road: we sell at 40 €/sqm, the first step, to whoever walks it

The thesis

We buy an option, not land

  • Notarised promise, price locked at 20 €/sqm; 10% deposit refundable on demand, secured by mortgage
  • At risk: only the operating budget, 5% of the acquisition value, for an upside 10–20 times larger
  • We create the added value ourselves: PUZ and masterplan, at a fixed cost known in advance
  • The classic model buys the whole plot and waits for the PUZ with the full price at risk; we control the land with 10% and do the work
  • At term: exit, extension of the option against a premium, or second-instalment financing — options written into the contract

Where the value comes from

  • Ready-to-build land: the buyer knows exactly what and how much can be built and can file for the building permit at once; it pays a premium for certainty and time
  • Not "a PUZ" but a masterplan calibrated to the area's developments, prepared by our strategic architect with full knowledge of the general urban plan, the infrastructure and real demand
  • Infrastructure (A0, the new runway, county roads) and the scarcity of regulated land lift the area's price while our entry price stays locked

Why the owner signs

  • The raw-land market is stuck: whoever buys today buys ready-to-build. Alone, the owner waits
  • A buyer who wants to develop needs clarity: what can be built, how much of the area is usable, how access and utilities are solved and how long until construction. That is exactly what we bring the owner
  • The owner does not fund the planning work and keeps title until purchase; in return he accepts a contractual lock on the land at an agreed price and term, with a refundable, secured deposit
  • If we buy, he collects his price; if the project stops, he refunds the deposit and keeps regulated land he can sell to anyone
  • The value comes from execution: plot selection, negotiation, planning coordination and shaping the product to buyer demand. That is how we raise the odds of a sale; we do not guarantee the outcome

Why RBI Land is aligned

  • 30% shareholder, with no share premium; it delivers the services out of the capped 5% budget, and collects its 30% share of the gain only after the investors' capital is returned in full
  • Fixed-price execution, known in advance; any overrun is RBI Land's
  • The interest is a good exit price, not duration; the permitting pace adapts to the market and to infrastructure progress, to monetise the maximum

How it works

five stages, two payments

For each stage: what the investor does, what RBI Land does and where the money is.

01 · NOWThe commitment 02 · INCORPORATIONThe company is set up 03 · PROMISE READY TO SIGNFunding and the promise 04 · MONTHS 1–18The zoning plan (PUZ) 05 · BY MONTH 26The exit
Investor Fills in the commitment form, with the amount. No money at this stage. Becomes a shareholder and pays in their part of the 10,000 lei share capital (≈ 2,000 €): 1,000 lei for every 10%. It covers the set-up costs and is the only amount paid before the call. When the promise is ready to sign, possibly weeks or months after incorporation, receives notice and pays in the amount within 7 days. Receives the monthly report on the portal and has access to the company's accounts. Receives their capital in full, then their share of the gain.
RBI Land Due diligence on the land, negotiation of the promise, the planner's quote. Is appointed director in the articles of association. Its contract is approved by the investors, with RBI Land abstaining. Signs the promise on behalf of the company, only after all the money is in. Delivers at a fixed price: planner, studies, permits, local council. Bears any overruns. Sells from 2× the investors' capital; between 1.5× and 2×, the shareholders decide by 2/3.
Money None. The share capital, in the company's account. Payment 1: the deposit to the landowner, when the promise is notarised. Payment 2: the operating budget to RBI Land, in five tranches, at the project stages: 40 / 25 / 20 / 7.5 / 7.5%; the last tranche at the council decision. RBI Land manages the budget at its own discretion, within the cap; that is why it can guarantee the fixed price. The buyer pays for the shares and takes over the balance of the land price.

How the budget is released to RBI Land

The 60,000 € + VAT go into the company's account at the single call and are released in five tranches, at verifiable stages. The first tranche also covers the company's start-up costs.

TrancheWhenAmountWhat it covers
40%At the signing of the promise, together with the deposit to the owner24,000 €notary, lawyer, land book; the planner's advance; topography, geotechnical; running the company: accounting, registered office, filings

Company – RBI Land contract: fixed price 66,300 €, of which 60,000 € + VAT from the investors; the difference and any overrun of the package, RBI Land. Each tranche is invoiced with VAT; the company recovers it.

What the 5% package includes

  • Everything in the table: planner, studies, official fees and permits, notary, accounting, coordination
  • Project management by RBI Land and the company's running costs for the whole term (accounting, registered office, filings, reporting)
  • Any overrun on the costs included in the package is borne by RBI Land. Exceptional costs outside RBI Land's control (new fees imposed by the authorities, a change of permitting route) are submitted for the investors' approval before any spending

What it does not include

  • The land price and the deposit: they are capital, not cost
  • The phase after exit: building permit, design, utility connections, roads
  • Notarial deeds for the share transfer at exit or for the land purchase (second instalment)
  • Each investor's own taxes
  • Selling costs at exit (intermediary, if any): deducted from the transfer price before distribution and approved together with the offer
  • Company formation: paid from the 10,000 lei share capital, paid in pro rata at incorporation

How the cap is protected

  • Fixed-price contract between the company and RBI Land, signed at formation
  • The budget sits in the company's account and is released to RBI Land in five tranches, at the project stages; RBI Land manages it at its own discretion, within the fixed cap
  • Exceptional fees imposed by the authorities or a change of route: RBI Land informs, documents and asks for the investors' approval before any spending

Formula: investors together hold 70% of the shares and put in 100% of the capital, so your share of capital = stake ÷ 70%. Minimum 10%, held for at least one year (the tax-exemption condition). VAT is recovered from the state, stays in the company, goes into the transfer price and returns at face value before the gain; returns are calculated on capital excluding VAT. Below the break-even the company does not sell: the loss remains the operating budget.

How it is calculated. Transfer price = exit price × 60,000 sqm − 1,080,000 € balance paid to the owner by the buyer. From it, the investors' capital is returned first: the 120,000 € deposit + the 60,000 € operating budget. Gain = transfer price − 180,000 €; 70% to investors, 30% to RBI Land. The VAT recovered (12,600 €) is added to the transfer price as the company's cash and returns to the investors before the gain. Your share of capital and of gain = stake ÷ 70%. Annual return = the multiple, annualised over the chosen duration. Selling costs at exit (intermediary, if any) are deducted from the transfer price when the offer comes and are not in the model. The figures in this paragraph are for the example plot; change the plot area and entry price above and the whole model recalculates for any plot.

The exit: who we sell to, and how

four routes, several buyers

The land stays locked for at least 12 months, while the PUZ is prepared and the area's value rises. We sell when the offer is good, before or after approval. What is sold is the company (the shares), not the land.

The option: what the company holds, when it is exercised, when it is lost

The company's asset is the purchase option: the notarised promise at 20 €/sqm, registered in the land book, with the deposit secured by mortgage. At exit, this option is sold through the transfer of the shares. The terms below are what we ask the owner for; the final form is shown before the decision to enter.

MomentRuleFor investors
At signingPrice locked at 20 €/sqm for the whole term. 10% deposit, refundable at the company's request, at any time, within 30 days, secured by a mortgage registered in the land book. Two distinct protections: if the owner changes his mind or breaches his obligations, he repays double the deposit; if he fails to refund the deposit on request within 30 days, he owes a penalty equal to the deposit, which also covers enforcement costs. Where negotiated, a transfer of the land in lieu of payment. Every negotiated protection is reflected in the promise and in the plot file, before the transaction.The deposit is contractually refundable and secured by a mortgage; the exposure is the operating budget.
From month 12The company may be sold: the buyer takes over the option and pays the balance to the owner, with or without the PUZ approved. Selling after one year secures the tax treatment of the transfer (0% for Romanian companies holding at least 10%).Capital back first, then 70% of the gain.
Month 18The base term. If the PUZ procedure is under way and the permits have been obtained, the 6-month extension applies automatically, at no cost. Otherwise the owner may terminate the promise and refund the deposit within 30 days; the company loses the option. Alternatively, the company may exercise the option and buy the land, with second-instalment financing.The decision to exercise the option belongs to the investors, with new capital; participation is optional.
After the council decision60 days to pay the balance, by the buyer of the company or from the second instalment. Without payment on time, the option is lost and the deposit is refunded on request within 30 days. The owner keeps the land and the approved PUZ, funded by the company.Until the decision, the company can be sold at any time; in practice the buyer is identified before approval.
Month 24 + 60 daysThe option's maximum term. Any extension beyond it is negotiated separately, against an additional premium.The investors decide, with new capital.
On stoppingThe refunded deposit and the unspent budget return to the company's account and are distributed to investors pro rata to their stake, through a capital reduction (share premium) or liquidation, under the articles of association. If the owner does not pay, the mortgage is enforced.The loss is the budget spent up to that point; the owner keeps the PUZ obtained on their land.

Decision points: what happens and who decides

The terms below (18 months + a 6-month extension + 60 days after the PUZ, 26 months at most) are what we ask the owner for. The final form depends on the negotiation with each owner and is shown to investors before the decision to enter. Once signed, no extension and no sale below the floor takes place without the investors' decision.

A transfer of shares to another shareholder is permitted at any time, at a negotiated price; to a third party, with the shareholders' consent and a right of first refusal at the same price.—
From month 12The one-year holding condition is met for all shareholders; a sale of the company becomes possible, with or without the PUZ approved, when the offer is good. The holding year runs from incorporation, so it is completed before month 12 of the project. With no buyer at a good price, the options are: extending the option by an addendum with the owner, against an additional premium justified by the area's infrastructure progress; or financing the second instalment (new investors, the same investors or debt) to buy the land and subdivide or develop.The investors, with new capital; participation is optional

Month 26, no buyer: we do not wait. If there is no interest, we withdraw, recover the deposit and close; the loss is the budget. If there is interest and potential (infrastructure advancing, buyers in discussion, an offer below the floor), the shareholders decide by vote: a sale below the floor, only if investors recover their capital, extending the option against the premium provided in the contract, refinancing or the second instalment. Every option is prepared in advance; none happens by default.

Continuation procedure, if it comes to that: at least 60 days before the maximum term, RBI Land presents within 15 days the proposed strategy, with the additional cost, the source of funding, the new term and the premium negotiated with the owner. Shareholders have 30 days to state their position and a further 10 days to pay in their pro-rata share. The new phase is financed through a capital increase at the company's market value after the PUZ; whoever does not take part owes nothing and keeps their shares, diluted at that value, and the new money has priority on repayment. Not taking part does not mean a buy-out. The continuation share may be taken up by the other shareholders or by RBI Land. The extension premium paid to the owner is, as a rule, non-refundable and is treated as a cost of the new phase. If nobody continues, the stop applies.

Exit rules

The thresholds measure what investors receive against the capital invested (excluding VAT, after sale costs), so they automatically reflect the land price and the deposit. The target price in the simulator (40 €/sqm) is the commercial objective; the thresholds below are the decision rules. Any shareholder may bring an offer; RBI Land presents every offer to the shareholders.

OfferOn the example plot (10% / 20% deposit)Who decides

Capital = what you paid in, excluding VAT (VAT comes back separately). 1.5× / 2× = how many times the exit returns your capital, after sale costs. Annual return = the same gain, per year; it depends on duration, which is why the rule uses the multiple.

A promise to sell the company may be signed before the PUZ approval or before the year is complete, with closing at term; the buyer's deposit sits in an escrow account and is not touched until the transfer. The promise follows the same voting rules as the sale.

Routes C and D are new investments with their own risk and timeline, presented separately if the shareholders decide to continue. Selling building land directly from the company carries VAT; a transfer of shares does not.

preliminary concept, to be fixed with the planner

The plot is proposed for residential use: a development of individual and small collective housing, with small retail and neighbourhood services on the ground floor (pharmacy, grocery, services), within the limits of the general urban plan and the planning certificate. The PUZ sets the exact proportions.

Houses and duplexes

Plots for detached houses and duplexes. The part that can be sold directly, plot by plot.

Small blocks, ground + 2

Low-rise, with ground-floor space for neighbourhood services.

Services and rent-producing space

Pharmacy, small retail, café, salon, spa, nursery or after-school, car wash, playground, sized to the plot. They make the area liveable, lift the price of every plot and give the buyer rental income as well, not only sales.

After approval, the land can be sold whole, to a developer, or subdivided, by zone. Details on the second instalment (T2) are in the section “Who buys at exit”.

A small circle of investors

For every plot, before any decision: legal due diligence (land book, encumbrances, litigation), planning (general urban plan, planning certificate, required permits, including AACR aeronautical restrictions), technical (access, utilities, survey) and financial (projections, comparables, sale floor). The plot file is presented to investors before formation; each decides plot by plot. This page is on the example plot and serves to validate the structure.

Land use is set plot by plot. The 19 plots do not all get the same use: depending on position (next to A0 and the express road, next to the airport, inside the village), size and what is already being built around, the PUZ proposes logistics, retail, mixed use or residential with small retail. On one of the plots the masterplan provides a piazza-type retail gallery, an anchor for the surrounding land. RBI Land tracks every development in the corridor and feeds it into the plan, so each plot gets the use the market pays best for. One PUZ = one company: each plot has its own company; adjoining plots, with a single PUZ and a single buyer, are grouped into one company.

Why the structure is built this way

tax, regulation, scale

The structure was designed after studying Romania's real-estate co-investment platforms and syndication models: we kept what protects the investor and avoided what adds compliance cost without value for a project with at most 8 shareholders (7 investors and RBI Land) and a single plot.

No tax at exit, under the current tax regime

  • The land is not sold; the shares are: no VAT, and the company realises no profit
  • A Romanian company holding at least 10% without interruption for at least one year pays no tax on the gain from selling the shares (Fiscal Code, art. 23 let. i)
  • That is why the minimum stake is 10% and a sale is possible from month 12
  • Investing through a company is recommended, not mandatory; individuals and non-residents: different treatment, check with your own adviser
  • The tax law in force at the date of exit applies; the current regime (Fiscal Code, art. 23 let. i) may change. Confirmed by written tax opinion before formation

How the money goes in and comes out

  • The project capital comes in at the call as share premium, through a capital increase with a token nominal (Companies Law no. 31/1990, art. 210 et seq.); the premium is booked in the company's equity, is not taxable income and is not a loan
  • Not being a loan, it does not fall under the ban on returning contributions in art. 67 and bears no interest; not being profit, it is not distributed as a dividend
  • At exit, the money reaches the shareholders through the transfer price, paid directly by the buyer; the company distributes nothing
  • On stopping, unused amounts are returned through a capital reduction with repayment of premiums (art. 207) or through liquidation
  • The tax advantages belong to the structure, not to an optimisation: a transfer of shares carries no VAT; the company realises no profit; the gain of a Romanian company holding at least 10% for one year is exempt (art. 23 let. i). All under the regime in force, confirmed by tax and legal opinion before formation

Built to scale

  • Every plot: the same structure, the same contracts, the same suppliers, a new company
  • 19 plots under review, 5–7 targeted; the investor enters where they want, with what they want, minimum 10%
  • RBI Land manages all the companies at a fixed price; reporting is identical
  • One investor may take the whole ticket of a plot; governance does not depend on percentages but on the articles of association and the shareholders' agreement

The structure and tax treatment are confirmed with the company's lawyer and tax adviser before formation; the written opinions go into the data room.

Who decides what

The rules are set once, at formation, and nobody can change them alone: neither the investors with 70%, nor RBI Land. Any change means a shareholders' resolution and an addendum to the articles of association.

Voting ruleDecisions
Unanimity (all shareholders, RBI Land included)changing the rules: articles of association, shareholders' agreement, management contract, thresholds, the 70/30 split · selling the company before one year · any partnership, transaction or asset outside the object (assigning the promise instead of the company, a second plot) · voluntary dissolution before term
2/3 of the votes (RBI Land votes)a sale between 1.5× and 2× capital · removing the director, on limited grounds, after a 30-day cure period · exceptional costs above the cap · extending the option against a premium · continuation after the maximum term · early stop
RBI Land alone, as directorexecution within the capped budget: suppliers, PUZ, permits, monthly reporting · presenting every offer · the sale from 2× capital
Each shareholder alonebringing exit offers · selling their stake: to another shareholder directly, to a third party with the shareholders' consent and first refusal · not taking part in a continuation, without losing what they hold

First refusal and notices. Whoever wants to sell to a third party notifies the company with the price and the buyer; the other shareholders have 15 days to exercise in writing their right to buy at the same price, pro rata. All notices between shareholders go by e-mail, to the addresses in the shareholders' agreement, and are posted on this page, on the notice board; the e-mail date is the notice date.

Reporting and transparency

Monthly report, on this page

A short report every month: what was done, what comes next, the bank statement. Each investor sees it here, with their own code. At each major milestone, a full management report. After the PUZ approval, an independent valuation report on the land, as the basis for the exit.

The project company's accounts

Tunari Land Invest 1's accounts are kept digitally, on the Keez platform. Every shareholder has access and can see at any time what has come into and gone out of the company's account. RBI Land keeps its own accounts separately.

Rules written from the start

The contract between the company and RBI Land states exactly when each tranche is released and on which document. The budget is capped at 5%; any exception is explained case by case, with documents.

Reports will appear on this page after the company is incorporated.

Risks and protections

The maximum loss is the operating budget, which is 5% of the land acquisition value (see terms). The deposit is contractually refundable, secured by mortgage, in every stop scenario.

What can happenWhat the company doesTotal loss
The zoning plan (PUZ) is rejected by the local councilAsks for the deposit back, which is refunded. The budget spent is lost.60,000 €
The project stops at any stage, for any reasonThe same mechanism. The loss does not grow over time.60,000 €
No buyer appears before the second instalment (T2)Walks away from the promise and recovers the deposit.60,000 €
It takes longer than 18 monthsThe budget is fixed. Profit in euros stays the same; only the annual return falls.0 €
Costs exceed the estimateFor investors the budget is capped at 5%. RBI Land pays the difference. Only new costs imposed by the authorities can exceed the cap, with justification and shareholder approval.0 €
An investor does not pay in on the callThey lose their place. The promise is not signed until all the money is in. RBI Land takes over their share capital at nominal value.0 €

The money stays put

Capital comes in as share premium. It can leave the company only through a capital reduction: unanimity and a two-month creditor objection period. No one, neither RBI nor any investor, can withdraw money along the way.

Two payments, nothing more

The company pays the deposit to the landowner and the RBI Land budget, in five tranches, at the project stages. It has no other suppliers: RBI Land pays operating costs from the budget.

What is not yet proven

The price of 40 €/sqm is a working assumption, supported by the buyer's calculation and plot prices in the area. The investment is illiquid until exit, and RBI Land sells without a vote only from 2× the investors' capital.

Questions every investor asks

Can I lose the 10% deposit?

No, contractually. The deposit is refundable at the company's request, at any time, within 30 days, and is secured by a mortgage registered in the land book. The deposit is secured by a mortgage; if the owner does not pay, the mortgage is enforced. Two distinct protections: if the owner changes his mind or breaches his obligations, he repays double the deposit; if he fails to refund the deposit on request, he owes a penalty equal to the deposit, which also covers enforcement costs. Where negotiated, a transfer of the land in lieu of payment. Every negotiated protection is reflected in the promise and in the plot file, before the transaction. The owner's side of the bargain: the company funds the PUZ, which stays with the land in any case.

Can I withdraw my money before exit?

No, and neither can the other shareholders. This protects you: the project cannot be stopped because one shareholder wants their money back. You can sell your stake to another shareholder at any time. To a third party, with the shareholders' consent and a 15-day right of first refusal for the other shareholders.

Who controls the company's account?

The director, RBI Land. The company has two accounts: the deposit account, with a single purpose (paying the owner) and joint signature, and the operating account, from which the tranches to RBI Land are released. Investors' money never goes into an RBI Land account. For the payment of the deposit to the owner, the one large payment, the payment order is signed jointly by RBI Land and a representative of the investors appointed by shareholders' resolution, and executed on the day of authentication, with proof of payment recorded in the deed. The capital call is made only once the promise is negotiated and the notary date is fixed, with 7 days to pay. Tranches to RBI Land are released at the project stages, on the director's instruction; the budget is at RBI Land's discretion, within the fixed cap, with no approval of individual expenses. You receive the monthly report on this page, the management report at each tranche and access to the company's digital accounting.

Why does RBI Land get 30%, and what does it put in?

RBI Land is a shareholder with 30% of the shares so that it benefits from the same tax treatment as the investors; it pays in its part of the share capital (3,000 lei) and no share premium; the 30% is of the profit, not of the capital: capital leaves first, back to those who put it in; the project capital is put in by the investors. At exit, the investors' share premium (their capital) is returned first, in full; what remains is split by shares, at the same price per share: 70% investors, 30% RBI Land. Because it brings the land, the negotiation, the structure and the delivery of the zoning plan (PUZ), and because it takes on the risk of cost overruns. RBI is paid last: investors' capital is returned in full first, and only then is the gain shared.

What does the operating budget cover, and why is it fixed?

The budget is capped at 5% of the acquisition value by the contract between the company and RBI Land, which also fixes when each instalment is released. The line-by-line breakdown, built on the quotes received, is in The operating budget, line by line. Anything above the cap is paid by RBI Land. Exceptional fees imposed by the authorities or a change of route are presented, documented and approved by the investors before any spending.

How do we know the land is worth 40 €/sqm after the PUZ?

We do not know exactly, and we do not rely on it. The investment is an option: at 30 €/sqm the profit is still several times the maximum loss (see the scenarios table), and break-even is 21 €/sqm. Before incorporation you receive the analysis of comparable transactions in the area and a case study of a similar plot taken by RBI through the same process. These set the minimum price below which the company cannot be sold.

How does the money come back at exit?

The company does not sell its land; the shareholders sell their shares. The buyer pays each shareholder directly, using the formula fixed in the articles of association at entry: first each investor's capital, in full, then the gain, 70% to investors and 30% to RBI. The money does not pass through the company's account, and there is no dividend distribution.

Why does capital come in as share premium?

Share capital stays small and the rest of the amount comes in as share premium. This keeps the company out of the situation covered by Article 67 of the Companies Law, and no one can take the money out along the way. If the project stops, the remaining amount is returned through a capital reduction or the liquidation of the company, under the procedure set out in the articles of association.

Why at least 10% and at least one year?

Because this way the money reaches you free of tax and VAT, legally. At exit the land is not sold; the company is. A transfer of shares carries no VAT, and the company does not realise the profit itself, so it pays no tax on it. For a Romanian company holding at least 10% of the company, without interruption, for at least one year, the gain on the sale of shares is not taxable. That is why every stake is at least 10%, and the sale takes place at least one year after entry. For individuals and foreign investors the treatment differs: check with your own tax adviser.

Why do we recommend investing through a company?

A Romanian company holding at least 10% for one year pays no tax on the gain from selling its shares. For stakes below 10%, or for individuals and non-residents, the tax treatment differs. Discuss the right option with your own tax adviser before committing.

What tax do I pay at exit?

For a Romanian company holding at least 10% of the company for one year, the gain on the sale of shares is not taxable. Individuals and non-residents are treated differently; we recommend investing through a Romanian company. Check with your own tax adviser.

What happens if the full capital is not raised?

The promise is not signed. There is no partial signing and no later capital calls. The company stays ready for the next plot or is dissolved, as the shareholders decide.

What happens if an investor does not pay in on the call?

They lose the right to participate, and their amount is taken up by the other investors or by RBI Land, on the same terms. Their part of the share capital is bought by RBI Land at nominal value, i.e. they get back exactly what they paid in. The mechanism is set out contractually: in the commitment letter, the articles of association and the shareholders' agreement, with an irrevocable mandate to sign the transfer.

What happens at month 12, and what can I do if I want out?

From month 12 a sale is possible for everyone. A stake can be sold at any time: to another shareholder, directly; to a third party, with the shareholders' consent and a 15-day right of first refusal for the others, at the same price. Whoever sells before one year loses only the tax exemption on their own gain; the others are not affected. Nobody can ask the company for their money back: that is what stops one shareholder from halting the project. The full timeline, with extensions and who decides, is in Decision points.

What exactly do we sell after one year, if the PUZ is not yet approved?

The purchase option: the notarised promise at 20 €/sqm, with the PUZ procedure under way and the permits obtained, through the transfer of the shares. The buyer takes over the company and pays the balance to the owner. Land with an approved PUZ is worth more than land with the procedure under way, but both sell; the timing follows the offer. Selling after one year secures the tax treatment of the transfer.

Who decides the sale, and when?

The sale can take place any time after month 12, once the one-year condition is met for everyone, and no later than month 26. We do not necessarily wait for the PUZ approval: if the offer is good, we sell. The rules are measured as a multiple of the investors' capital and written into the articles of association and the management contract: below 1.5× there is no sale; between 1.5× and 2× a sale is approved by 2/3 of the votes; from 2×, RBI Land sells and all shareholders sell together, on the same terms. Any shareholder may bring offers, RBI Land presents them all. Before one year, only by unanimity.

Your questions

published here, for everyone

Questions sent through the form, on WhatsApp or at the joint session are answered in writing, in this section, for all investors at once. Terms stay identical for everyone.

Questions received while preparing the round · 2 October

Can two plots go into the same company?

No. One plot, one company. That keeps each plot's risk isolated, the exit separate and the decision plot by plot. The next opportunities come as new companies with the same structure.

If I hold 30%, do I have a veto?

There is no individual veto. From 2× capital, RBI Land accepts the offer and everyone sells together; between 1.5× and 2×, the shareholders decide by 2/3; below 1.5× there is no sale. The rule protects the project from deadlock and every investor from a sale that is too cheap.

Can I invest as an individual?

Yes, but the tax treatment differs: for individuals the gain on the sale of shares is taxed, whereas a Romanian company holding at least 10% for one year pays no tax on it. We recommend investing through a company; check with your own tax adviser.

What if RBI Land does not deliver?

The contract between the company and RBI Land has a fixed price and instalments released only at verifiable stages; the money sits in the company's account, not with RBI Land. The promise, the mortgage and all documents are in the company's name. The director can be removed only for fraud or a serious, proven breach of the management contract, after a 30-day cure period, by a two-thirds majority of the shareholders' votes; refusing to present the shareholders an offer above the floor is such a breach. The reason: RBI Land holds ongoing contracts with the planner and other suppliers; on removal, the new director takes them over by negotiation.

Who pays if the PUZ costs more than the budget?

RBI Land. The 5% cap on the acquisition value is fixed in the contract; any overrun of the package is RBI Land's. The only exception: exceptional fees imposed by the authorities or a change of route, which are presented, documented and approved by the investors before any spending.

What stops the owner selling to someone else meanwhile?

The promise is notarised and registered in the land book, and the deposit is secured by mortgage. A sale to anyone else is blocked by the registration; if the owner breaches the promise, the deposit is repaid double.

Can I exit early by selling my stake to RBI Land?

You can sell at any time to another shareholder, RBI Land included, at a negotiated price. RBI Land does not guarantee a buy-back: an on-demand exit right could halt the project for everyone else. To third parties, after 12 months, with first refusal for the shareholders.

Why not buy the land outright?

For the same gain you would need ten times the capital, locked for two years, with the PUZ risk on the full price. The option with a refundable deposit limits the maximum loss to the operating budget, 5% of the acquisition value.

When do I see the real plot, the documents and the quotes?

After the confidentiality agreement, before formation: the plot sheet, the land-book extract, supplier quotes, the comparables analysis and the Petricani case with the notarial deeds. Today's commitment is on the structure; the final decision is taken on the plot.

What do I receive monthly?

A short report on this page: the stage we are at, money spent against budget, next steps and deadlines. Plus access to the company's digital accounting (Keez) and the management report at each instalment release.

no money, no obligation

Terms used on this page

  

    
      
Land acquisition valueThe price agreed with the landowner in the promise to sell: area × price per sqm. On the reference plot: 60,000 sqm × 20 €/sqm = 1,200,000 €. The deposit (10%) and the operating budget (5%) are both calculated on it.

      
Deposit10% of the acquisition value on the example plot; depending on the plot, between 10% and 20%, set in the plot sheet. Paid to the landowner when the promise is signed. Refundable on the company's demand, secured by a mortgage.

      
Operating budgetThe amount capped at 5% of the acquisition value, paid by the company to RBI Land in five tranches (40 / 25 / 20 / 7.5 / 7.5%), for the PUZ, studies, permits, notary, accounting and coordination. It is the only amount investors can lose.

      
Investor capitalDeposit + operating budget (+ recoverable VAT on the budget). On the reference plot: 192,600 €. Returned in full, first, at exit.

      
ExitThe sale of the company's shares to a buyer, who pays the shareholders and takes over the balance of the land price owed to the landowner. The land is not sold; the company is.

      
Exit price (€/sqm)The value the buyer places on the land when buying the company. Share price = exit price × area − balance owed to the landowner.

      
GainWhat remains of the transfer price after the investors have received their share premium (capital) back, in full. Split by shares, at the same price per share: 70% investors, 30% RBI Land.

      
Operating packageThe services RBI Land delivers to the company at a fixed price, within the operating budget: planner and PUZ, studies, official fees, notary, accounting, coordination and reporting; formation is paid from the share capital, preparing the sale. Detailed in The operating budget.

      
Sale thresholdsMinimum floor = investors receive at least 1.5× their capital (below it, no sale). Automatic sale threshold = at least 2× capital (from there, RBI Land sells and everyone sells together). In between, 2/3 of the votes. Measured on capital excluding VAT, after sale costs; written into the articles of association and the management contract.

      
MultipleHow many times the exit returns the capital you paid in (excluding VAT, after sale costs). 2× = you put in 100, you receive 200. The sale thresholds are measured on it.
Annual returnThe same gain, per year (IRR). 2× over 18 months ≈ 59% a year; 2× over 24 months ≈ 41% a year. It depends on duration, so it is not used as a rule.
Right of first refusalThe other shareholders' right to buy, at the same price and pro rata, the stake an investor wants to sell to a third party. Exercised in writing within 15 days of the e-mail notice; a sale to a third party requires the shareholders' consent.

      
Option extensionAn addendum with the owner, after month 24, against a new premium, to keep the right to buy. Decided by the investors and financed with new money; nobody is obliged to take part.

      
Share capital10,000 lei (≈ 2,000 €) in total: 7,000 lei from the investors (1,000 lei for every 10% of the company) and 3,000 lei from RBI Land, for 30%. Paid in within 7 days of the Q&A session, by all shareholders, as the firm commitment; smaller amounts are not accepted. It covers formation. The project capital comes in at the call, from the investors only, as share premium, through a token nominal increase. If the plot is not bought after all, this is all that is lost.

            
Capital callThe only request to pay in: made when the promise is ready to sign, with 7 days to pay. The promise is signed only once all the capital is in the company's account.

      
Break-evenThe exit price at which investors recover exactly their capital: 21 €/sqm on the reference plot. Below it, the company does not sell.
